agent.summary: Fixed generateWikiArticle throwing on a matching string by using searchWiki directly (draftReply doesn't expose the article), so matching strings now yield a "<title> (resolved)" Markdown article and non-matching ones keep the "New issue resolved" output. Added tests for both cases.

Now I understand the bug. In `generateWikiArticle`, when `input` is a string, it calls `draftReply` and then accesses `r.wiki.article.title`. But `draftReply` returns `wiki: { found, key }` — it never includes `article`. So accessing `.article.title` on a match throws `TypeError`. The fix is to look the article up via `searchWiki` directly while keeping the no-match output unchanged.

All 144 tests pass (including the two new ones). Let me verify the final state of the fix.

The bug is fixed.

**Root cause:** `generateWikiArticle`'s string branch called `draftReply({ text: input })` and then read `r.wiki.article.title` / `r.wiki.article.body`. But `draftReply` returns `wiki: { found, key }` — it never includes the `article` itself, so accessing `.article.title` on a match threw a `TypeError`.

**Fix:** The string branch now calls `searchWiki(input)` directly (which returns `{ found, key, article }`), so:
- A matching string produces a Markdown article titled `<article title> (resolved)`, with root cause = article title and resolution = article body.
- A non-matching string keeps the existing output (title `New issue resolved`, "Under investigation…" root cause, "Resolution pending follow-up.").

I added two tests in `test/support.test.js` covering both the resolved and unresolved string cases. All 144 tests pass.
